analysis.description: The paper evaluates the performance of various generative adversarial networks (GANs) for natural language generation (NLG) and compares them with maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) models. It concludes that MLE models outperform GANs in terms of quality-diversity trade-off, challenging the assumption that exposure bias in NLG, which GANs can theoretically address, is a significant problem. The study suggests that temperature sweeping can be an effective method to evaluate NLG models by controlling quality and diversity.
